title: API gateway: routing rules, streaming proxy buffer tuning, and payload size limits for OpenAI-compat tool calls
author: Ravi Menon
description: Motivation: Production incidents showed increased tail latency and occasional request truncation for streaming responses when customers used OpenAI-compat tool/function calling with large tool payloads. This PR consolidates a set of API-gateway performance tweaks to improve streaming stability and preserve the OpenAI-compat behavior while enforcing pragmatic payload limits. Changes: 1) Introduces a routing policy update to prefer local-region dedicated backends for tool-calls and to fall back to the 'compat' pool only when feature flags allow it. 2) Adds adaptive streaming proxy buffers with per-route caps tuned from production telemetry; buffers shrink when per-client concurrency is high and grow for low-concurrency stable streams. 3) Enforces new soft payload size limits for tool/function call bodies (default 512KB) with clear 413 responses and an opt-in larger limit via tenant config for Dedicated customers. 4) Ensures structured output passthrough (json/tool-results) remains unchanged for OpenAI-compat responses and adjusts chunking to avoid JSON splits across buffer boundaries. 5) Adds detailed telemetry (buffer occupancy, chunking events, route fallback counts) and dashboards. Compatibility and migration: Default behavior is backward compatible for most customers; clients sending >512KB tool payloads will now receive a 413 unless their tenant has bump configured. Streaming semantics for normal generation unchanged; only tool-calls and high-payload streaming paths are affected. Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout targeting 10% of traffic for 48h, expand to 50% after monitoring, then global. See linked Linear tickets ENG-1982 and ENG-2035 for rollout automation. Testing: unit and integration tests added for buffer boundaries and JSON chunking; e2e verified against OpenAI-compat tool-call test suite. See notes and test matrix below.
